_comment: Prince Edward Island province page. No city page under it and there should not be one: the whole province is a single market of 154,331 people. This is the page that says outright that paid search is often the wrong tool here, which is also the strongest argument that this set of pages is not a doorway farm. Population and growth are from the StatCan Focus on Geography page cited at the bottom.

en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing across {city}
market: I will start with the part most consultants skip. {city} has 154,331 people, which for many local services means the monthly search volume is small enough that Google Ads cannot spend a sensible budget without buying searches that were never going to convert. If you sell to Islanders only, there is a real chance that paid search is the wrong tool for you, and I would rather tell you that on a free call than take $1,500 a month to run a campaign against demand that does not exist.

What does work here is being the obvious answer. In a market this size the shortlist for any service is genuinely short, so ranking well organically or being the business a chatbot names is worth disproportionately more than it would be in a city. Both of those are achievable on {city} budgets in a way that outbidding competitors is not.

The exception is anything that sells beyond the Island. Tourism reaches the whole country and further, and {industries} include several sectors whose customers are nowhere near here. If that is your business, the market is not 154,331 people and the advice above reverses completely: paid search becomes viable, because you are buying attention where the volume actually is.

en.servicesHeading: Three ways to grow a {city} business, run by one accountable person
en.servicesIntro: Same three services everywhere I work. In {city} the first question is which of them your numbers actually support, and the answer is not always all three.

services.title: Google Ads Management
services.body: Worth doing if you sell beyond the Island, or if you are in a category with real local urgency. Not worth doing for many Island-only services, and I will say so before you spend anything. Where it fits: account structure, targeting, and cutting spend on searches that were never going to convert.

services.title: SEO Consulting
services.body: Usually the right first investment here. A province-wide organic position is genuinely achievable at this size, and it keeps producing without a monthly media budget behind it. Technical fixes first, then the pages that answer what your customers are actually asking.

services.title: AIO Consulting
services.body: The best value of the three in a market this size. When someone asks ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google's AI Overviews for a business in {city}, it names a handful. Being one of them is a one-time piece of work and it does not care how small the search volume is.

area.districtsBody: I take on clients throughout {districts}. Everything is run remotely over video and email, so where on the Island you are makes no difference to the work or the price. There is no separate page for Charlottetown or Summerside because the whole province is one market and splitting it would be a fiction.
area.nearbyBody: I work with businesses in {nearby} on the same terms.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: Is our market too small for Google Ads?
faq.a: For a lot of Island-only businesses, honestly yes. There is not always enough monthly search volume to justify a management fee on top of the spend, and pretending otherwise would be selling you a service you do not need. If you sell beyond the Island, the answer flips and paid search becomes one of the better options available to you.

faq.q: So what should we do instead?
faq.a: Usually SEO and AIO. Both are about being the obvious answer rather than about buying attention by the click, and both work better the smaller and more concentrated the market is. In a province of this size, being the named recommendation is worth more than any budget you could reasonably spend on ads.

faq.q: Why is there no page for Charlottetown?
faq.a: Because Charlottetown and the rest of the province are not separate search markets in any way that would change my advice. Publishing a page for each town to catch each set of searches is the kind of thing that makes these pages worthless, so I have not done it.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
